column1: # TITLE: Gene expression from paired biopsies from a patient with METex14 skiping non-small cell lung cancer before and after treatment with neoadjuvant tepotinib (42 days)

# SUMMARY: Background: MET inhibitors have demonstrated efficacy in treating patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) harboring METex14 skipping alterations. Advancements in spatial profiling technologies have unveiled the complex dynamics of the tumor microenvironment
column2: a crucial factor in cancer progression and therapeutic response. Using spatial profiling
column3: this study investigates the effects of the MET inhibitor tepotinib on the TME in a case of locally advanced NSCLC with a METex14 skipping alteration. Methods: A patient with resectable stage IIIB NSCLC
column4: unresponsive to neoadjuvant platinum-based doublet chemotherapy
column5: received tepotinib following detection of a METex14 skipping alteration. Paired pre- and post-treatment biopsies were subjected to GeoMx Digital Spatial Profiling using the Cancer Transcriptome Atlas and immune-related protein panels to evaluate shifts in the tumor immune microenvironment (TIME). Results: Tepotinib administration resulted in pathological downstaging to stage IA1
column6: which allowed for a successful lobectomy and evidenced a significant pathological response. The TIME was transformed from an immunosuppressive to a more permissive state
column7: with upregulation of antigen-presenting and pro-inflammatory immune cells. Moreover
column8: a marked decrease in immune checkpoint molecules
column10: was noted. Spatial profiling identified discrete immune-enriched clusters
column11: indicating the role of tepotinib in modulating immune cell trafficking and function. Conclusions: Tepotinib appears to remodel the TIME in a patient with METex14 skipping NSCLC
column12: possibly increasing responsiveness to immunotherapy. This case supports the integration of genetic profiling into the management of early and locally advanced NSCLC to guide personalized
column13: targeted interventions. These findings highlight the need to further evaluate combinations of MET inhibitors and immunotherapies.
